title: Altars as tombs, yet every altar sanctified to Mary and all Saints; temples as basilicas
source_text: VI. Similiter, quamvis altaria, sub altarium ratione, ex Scholae Romanae doctrina, Sanctis proprie consecranda non sint, ostendimus tamen illius doctores existimare quod possint, sub ratione saltem tumuli, illis consecrari: imo, juxta praxin Ecclesiae Romanae, altaria singula sanctificari, non solum in honorem Dei, sed etiam in honorem Beatae Virginis, & omnium Sanctorum: ac eodem modo templa, ex illius Ecclesiae sententia atque usu, non praecise qua talia Sanctis esse construenda; sed tamen illis extrui & dicari posse ac debere, sub ratione aedium sacrarum, & Basilicarum, in quibus solemniter, & variis ritibus colantur, atque invocentur.
pass_a_gloss: Likewise, although altars, under the notion of altars, are not, by the doctrine of the Roman School, properly to be consecrated to the Saints, we showed nevertheless that its doctors think they can be consecrated to them at least under the notion of a tomb: indeed, according to the practice of the Roman Church, each altar is sanctified not only in honor of God but also in honor of the Blessed Virgin and of all the Saints; and in the same way temples, by the opinion and use of that Church, are not to be built for the Saints precisely as temples, yet can and ought to be raised and dedicated to them under the notion of sacred buildings and basilicas, in which they are solemnly cultivated and invoked with various rites.
pass_b_english: Rome's doctors will not consecrate an altar to a Saint as an altar, but they will as a tomb.
In practice every altar is sanctified to God and also to the Virgin and all the Saints.
Temples are not built for Saints precisely as temples, yet they are raised and dedicated as sacred houses and basilicas where Saints are ritually honored and invoked.

lemmas.gloss: under the notion of a tomb

choices.why: Bellarmino's workaround: a basilica is a shrine, not a temple of sacrifice.
